cells.remarks: On the stone, the figure of a hero is carved facing left. He holds a bow in his left hand and a short sword (kuraval) in his right hand. Near his left leg are a simil and a kendi, and near his right leg is a dog in a waiting posture. Inscriptions are engraved on the upper part and the right side of the figure. Two toranas (arches) are present on the upper part of the figure. The upper portion records that in the thirty-fourth regnal year of the Pallava king Mahendravarman I, Karundevakkathi, the young son of Potrokkaiyar who was the nephew (sister's son or relative) of the Bana king, died a hero's death protecting his buffalo. On the right side, it records that a dog named Govivan bit two thieves and stood guard.

cells.remarks: The figure of the hero is carved facing straight, holding a shield in the left hand and a sword in the right hand. Letters are engraved on the upper part of the figure. It records that when Tholtevar, the king of Mel-Kondrainadu, invaded during the twenty-first regnal year of the king named Somasikotiruman, Sevakanthan, a subordinate chief (mar-atiraisar), attained heroic death in battle. Mel-Kondrainadu Puliyur is mentioned in the Siniyanpettai inscription (of Kampavarman).
